chunks: Muhammad ibn Umar al-Hafith narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Hafs narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Ismail narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Salama, from Abu al-Sadiq. He said:

Ali (peace be upon him) said: My religion is the religion of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and my lineage is the lineage of the Prophet. So whoever attacks my religion and my lineage has surely attacked the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family).

key_terms.تناول: To attack, insult, or transgress against someone's honor or standing
key_terms.حسب: Lineage, honor, tribal prestige, noble ancestry — a key social value in pre-Islamic and early Islamic Arabia
key_terms.دين: Religion, faith, way of life — encompasses creed, practice, and identity

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about his relationship to the Prophet's religion and lineage?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) asserts that his religion and noble lineage are identical to those of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), establishing an inseparable bond between them. This statement was addressed to those who might question Ali's religious authority or ancestral honor, clarifying that any attack on Ali is equivalent to an attack on the Prophet himself. The original audience would have understood 'hasab' (حسب) as encompassing tribal honor, noble descent, and personal merit — all of which Ali shared with the Prophet through their common Hashimite lineage.
